gaps.explanation: can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.

gaps.sentence: He suggested ___ a taxi instead of walking.
gaps.explanation: suggest + -ing (no infinitive with a person: suggest that we take is also possible).

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.

gaps.sentence: He'd sooner ___ than ask for directions.
gaps.explanation: would sooner + bare infinitive (like would rather): sooner drive.

gaps.sentence: The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).

gaps.sentence: If you keep ___ like this, you'll exhaust yourself.
gaps.explanation: keep (+ on) is followed by -ing: keep working.
